raw_plan.root_cause: The function allocates a fixed 16-byte heap buffer with malloc(0x10) but then copies strlen(input)+1 bytes into it via memcpy without checking that the input length fits within the 16-byte allocation, allowing an oversized input to overflow the heap buffer.
raw_plan.original_behavior: Allocates 16 bytes via malloc; exits(1) if allocation fails; computes strlen(input)+1; memcpy's that many bytes from input into the 16-byte buffer; calls puts on the buffer; frees the buffer; returns. For inputs of length >= 16 this overflows the heap buffer.
raw_plan.required_invariant: At most 15 bytes (capacity-1) plus a NUL terminator may be written into the 16-byte heap buffer; the copy length must be min(strlen(input)+1, 16).
raw_plan.repair_strategy: After computing strlen(input)+1 in rdx, clamp the copy length to at most 16 (capacity) before calling memcpy, so the destination buffer is never overflowed; keep the malloc, null-check/exit, puts, free, and return sequence unchanged. For valid inputs (length <= 15) behavior is identical.
raw_plan.failure_behavior: If malloc returns NULL, call exit(1) as in the original. For oversized inputs, truncate the copy to 16 bytes (15 data bytes plus NUL) instead of overflowing; no crash or memory corruption occurs.
raw_plan.expected_behavior: For inputs of length <= 15, the full string is copied and printed via puts, then freed, matching original observable behavior. For inputs of length >= 16, only the first 15 bytes plus NUL are copied and printed, preventing the heap overflow while preserving the hi output path.
verification_conditions: Function terminates with ret at 0x401262.
Only direct calls to 0x4010f0 (malloc), 0x4010c0 (strlen), 0x4010e0 (memcpy), 0x4010b0 (puts), 0x4010a0 (free), 0x401100 (exit) are emitted.
memcpy length argument is clamped to <= 16 before the call at 0x401243.
For input length 15, output equals input and no overflow occurs.
For input length 16 or greater, at most 16 bytes are written to the heap buffer and no heap corruption occurs.
malloc failure path still calls exit(1).
